recordSchemas._rule: Every record that crosses a persistence or module boundary is closed. An unknown field is a contract violation with a deterministic outcome code, not an ignored extra. Absence from a field list is NOT closure — the checker rejects unknown keys mechanically.

EvidenceBundle.forbiddenFieldsWhy: Attempt metadata, process identity, timestamps and cache/lifetime state must not enter a semantic commitment unless a binding contract explicitly requires them. None does.

EvaluationEvidence.forbiddenFieldsWhy: E3 — proof adequacy is host-owned. A producer may submit a candidate but may not select a weaker obligation or declare its own output adequate.

ContentRef.rule: No bare boolean, bare string digest, or presence-only object satisfies a reference obligation.

ProofRelationshipMatch.forbiddenFieldsWhy: spanAnchor is forbidden here so a relationship claim cannot be dressed up as a located one (R3-PROBE-01).

ProofNoMatch.forbiddenFieldsWhy: The removed transitional shortcuts. Their presence is now a deterministic unknown/forbidden-field violation, not a silently accepted alternative (R3-PROBE-03).

invariants.assert: A clean authoritative verdict requires a non-empty required universe and exact member-set activation whose commitment recomputes.
Every proof reference is a resolvable ContentRef. Relationship claims require an ordered edge witness; a span alone never satisfies one.
Proof adequacy is host-owned; a producer may not declare its own obligation or adequacy.
An incomplete, sampled or truncated witness cannot support a complete or absence claim.
The verdict recomputes its outcome-set commitment over every activated evaluation under the canonical grammar.
No durable user-derived write occurs before storage root, privacy class and retention policy are resolved.
Every proof reference maps to exactly one retention unit at the minimum capability that needs it, and the closure commitment recomputes.
A replayable Run retains a non-empty offline-resolvable derivation closure.
An indeterminate or error outcome can never be absorbed into an authoritative pass.
A committed subject or member set recomputes from the retained fact partition; cardinality agreement is not set agreement.
Coverage, baseline, waivers and policy are resolvable content-addressed verdict inputs; absence must be explicit.
A unit is available only if every object it contains is available; effective capability is derived from current availability while sealed capability stays immutable.

providerMay: submit an evaluation candidate with its proof material
providerMayNot: choose a retention unit or custody strategy
authorityAndLayering.why: Attempt metadata varies between attempts that must produce identical semantic identity. Admitting it into a commitment would make replay and comparison impossible and would leak operational identity into a durable record.

assurance.why: A contract plus a retained checker is design-integrity evidence. AS-1: implementable:true performs no assurance transition. Nothing here is QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED and no product gate is unblocked.

retainedResiduals.statement: No-match fold plus reverification cost including retained fact custody is unmeasured. No constant-size or orders-of-magnitude claim is authorized.
evidence.v2 and check-evidence.py share an author with the Phase-1A artifacts they consume. Independent review by an agent that authored none of them is required before any seal.
evaluation-proof.v1 and retention-tiers.v6 remain CANDIDATE-AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW. If either changes, this contract's joins must be re-derived.
CD-RT-5 remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A. Evidence v2 records no product acceptance.

knownLimitations: Same-author risk across the whole Phase 1A/1B chain: proof contract, custody contract, evidence contract and all four checkers share one author.
Resolvability is modelled as membership in a declared objectStore. It does not prove a real content-addressed store returns those bytes.
The capability closure is validated for exactness but its recomputation cost at realistic unit counts is unmeasured.
Coverage is joined by identity and reference. Whether the Coverage object itself is sufficient for a given predicate remains FACT-PLANE's C-1 question, not this contract's.
Historical predicate semantics must stay rehydratable for later verification; that is a VERSIONING dependency this contract requires but does not answer.
sealRecommendation: DO NOT SEAL. Requires independent re-review by an agent that authored neither this contract, its checker, nor the Phase-1A artifacts it consumes.
